cohort: The study included singleton live births from 1997 through 2022 by mothers with Crohn's disease and previous perianal surgery.
finding: Vaginal delivery was not associated with increased important adverse maternal outcomes in mothers with Crohn's disease and prior perianal surgery.
mod_finding: Women who delivered vaginally had significantly less new perianal surgery within 12 months compared to those who delivered by c-section, with no significant differences in other measured adverse outcomes.
